# Town of Brookline municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 4; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): lists five Brookline Selectboard members: Emily Beer, E. Mark Bills, Michael Desocio (Chair), Bruce Mello, and Douglas Wellman.

Town of Brookline official website, Elected Town Officers page: lists the Selectboard as Michael Desocio (Chair; term to 2028), Doug Wellman (Vice Chair; term to 2027), Bruce Mello (term to 2029), Emily Beer (term to 2027), and E. Mark Bills (term to 2028).
Town of Brookline official website, Elected Town Officers page: lists Marjorie Ray as Town Clerk, elected, one-year term expiring 2027.
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, & County Clerks' (January 2026): lists Marjorie Ray as Town Clerk of Brookline.
Town of Brookline official website, Elected Town Officers page: lists Melissa Brown as Treasurer, appointed, term expiring 2027.
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, & County Clerks' (January 2026): lists Melissa Brown as Treasurer of Brookline.
Town of Brookline official website, Elected Town Officers page: lists David Y. Parker, Jr. as Moderator, elected, one-year term expiring 2027.

Town of Brookline official website, Elected Town Officers page: lists the Lister office with one seat 'Vacant' (term expiring 2029) and Helen Holt, appointed, term expiring 2027. The third seat is accounted for in no official source and is left unfilled.
Town of Brookline official website, Elected Town Officers page: lists three Auditors, all elected: Heidi Nystrom (Chair; term to 2027), Kendra Brooks (term to 2029), and Frank Rucker (term to 2027).

Town of Brookline official website, Elected Town Officers page: lists Melissa Brown as Delinquent Tax Collector, appointed, one-year term expiring 2027; the town fills the office separately, so the post is created under 17 V.S.A. section 2651d.

Town of Brookline official website, Elected Town Officers page: lists the First Constable officeholder as 'Selectboard' (the board itself), term printed 2026. No individual holder is named, so no membership is recorded. Structure only.

Town of Brookline official website, Elected Town Officers page: lists the Second Constable officeholder as 'Selectboard' (the board itself), term printed 2026. No individual holder is named, so no membership is recorded. Structure only.

Town of Brookline official website, Elected Town Officers page: lists five Cemetery Commissioner seats (five-year terms, all elected): Dorothy Maggio (term to 2030), Howard Osgood (term to 2031), one seat 'Vacant' (term to 2028), Michael W. Winot (term to 2027), and Doug Wellman (term to 2029). The vacant seat is left unfilled.

Town of Brookline official website, Elected Town Officers page: lists a single Trustee of Public Funds position, marked appointed, with the name cell blank (24 V.S.A. section 2431 permits a town to elect one or more trustees). No holder is named, so no membership is recorded. Structure only.

17 V.S.A. section 2646 (official text, Vermont General Assembly) provides for the election of a grand juror at annual town meeting. Structure only: no official source publishes the current holder; the seat is left unfilled rather than guessed.

17 V.S.A. section 2646 (official text, Vermont General Assembly) provides for the election of a town agent at annual town meeting. Structure only: no official source publishes the current holder; the seat is left unfilled rather than guessed.

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, '2025-2026 Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists two Brookline justices of the peace: Laurie J. Nau-Martocci and Dorothy Maggio.

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, '2025-2026 Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists two Brookline justices of the peace for the 2025-2026 term; they are the winners of the November 5, 2024 election for the office. The listing names only two justices for Brookline; any remaining seat is a possible vacancy the listing does not explain. The listing publishes no vote totals and no party designations for justices of the peace.
